column3: Description
Riding or performing a trick using the heelside edge of the board, leaning back on your heels toward the water.
Riding or performing a trick using the toeside edge of the board, leaning forward on your toes toward the water.
A spin where, during the first 90 degrees of rotation, you face toward the boat or cable line.
A spin where, during the first 90 degrees of rotation, you face away from the boat or cable line.
A trick performed while keeping the board in constant contact with the water.
Rotating the board frontside 90 degrees so it faces up the line while sliding along the water.
Rotating the board backside 90 degrees so it faces away from the line while sliding along the water.
A jump where the board leaves the water without the help of a wake, kicker, or obstacle.
Any trick or ollie where the rider reaches down and grabs the edge of the board.
Riding with your non-dominant foot forward (for example, if you usually ride left foot forward, switch would be right foot forward).
Landing or riding in switch stance after starting in your natural stance.
Landing with the handle held behind your back after completing the last half of a backside rotation.
Passing the handle from one hand to the other, usually behind the back, during a trick.
Approaching a spin with the handle already wrapped around your back before takeoff.
A handle pass trick where the handle is passed between the rider’s legs.
A spin trick where the rope is lifted over the rider’s head instead of passing the handle behind the back.
Spinning while keeping the board perpendicular to the water.
Spinning with the body tilted so that the board is not perpendicular to the water, giving a corked or laid-out appearance.
A 180-degree spin that changes your stance direction; can be frontside or backside.
A 360-degree spin (one full rotation); can be frontside or backside and often involves a handle pass.
A 540-degree spin (one and a half rotations); can be frontside or backside and often involves a handle pass.
A 720-degree spin (two full rotations); can be frontside or backside and often involves a handle pass.
A 900-degree spin (two and a half rotations); can be frontside or backside and often involves a handle pass.
A 1080-degree spin (three full rotations); can be frontside or backside and often involves a handle pass.
A 1260-degree spin (three and a half rotations); can be frontside or backside and often involves a handle pass.
A 1440-degree spin (four full rotations); can be frontside or backside and often involves a handle pass.
A trick where the rider changes the rotation direction mid-air, for example, frontside 360 followed by a backside 180.
From a heelside edge, the board is kicked out behind the rider and above the water, with the body extended like Superman.
Performed off a kicker, where the board swings forward over the rider’s head in a laid-out Superman position.
